summary: 交换建立在人能记住互惠关系的能力上。南非遗址的颜料和贝壳珠提示，人类珍视装饰品的历史可能远早于旧估计；稀缺物品也能传递身份和地位。

paragraphs.brief: 互惠与心中记账催生贸易
sentences: Humans are born to trade and we don’t need shops or money to do it—the heart of commerce is an instinctive ability for what anthropologists call “reciprocity”.
人类天生就会交易，无须商店或货币也能进行；商业的核心是人类学家所谓的“互惠”本能。

This is an ability to exchange goods of equal worth, and it evolved as the brains of our ancient ancestors and societies became more complex, allowing individuals to keep a running tally of their interactions with others.
这是一种交换等值物品的能力，它随着祖先大脑和社会日渐复杂而演化，使人能够记住自己与别人的来往。
Evidence from modern hunter-gatherers leaves little doubt that the exchange of food and favours is innate, as is the ability to keep track of the credits and debits that accrue as a result.
现代狩猎采集者的行为有力支持这样一种观点：互换食物、帮忙并记住由此积累的人情收支，都是人类与生俱来的能力。
Combine this skill for mental book-keeping with even the most basic material culture, and trade inevitably follows.
只要把这种心中记账的本领与哪怕最基本的物质文化结合起来，贸易便自然产生。
paragraphs.gist: 作者认为交易的根本在于天生的互惠能力：人能记住与他人互换物品或人情的得失，哪怕没有商店和货币也会发生贸易。

paragraphs.brief: 从生活必需品到无形价值
sentences: Once trade gets off the ground, the economic benefits quickly make it irresistible.
贸易一旦开展，它带来的经济利益很快就让人难以抗拒。
But exchanging tools, food and other essentials of life in a barter economy is a far cry from the shopping mall.
但是，在易货经济中交换工具、食物和其他生活必需品，与购物中心相去甚远。
Modern consumerism extends beyond subsistence and utilitarianism to encompass everything from Gucci handbags and BMW convertibles to valuable paintings.
现代消费早已越过生存和实用需要，涵盖古驰手袋、宝马敞篷车和昂贵画作等种种物品。
Clearly, the worth of such goods is not inherent but resides in certain intangible qualities that we invest in them.
这些商品的一部分价值显然并非与生俱来，而来自我们赋予它们的无形意义。
When did humans start holding these goods in such high esteem?
人类是从何时开始如此看重这些东西的？
paragraphs.gist: 以物易物能满足生存需要，但名牌手袋、名车和艺术品的身价还取决于人赋予它们的无形意义，由此引出消费文化的起源问题。

paragraphs.brief: 赭石颜料暗示早期象征需求
sentences: All the archaeological evidence for the flowering of consumer culture has up to now pointed to a date of around 40,000 years ago.
此前，消费文化兴盛的考古证据都指向约四万年前。

That’s when early modern humans started making increasingly intricate bone and stone tools, carving patterns into rocks and creating representational art such as carved figurines, jewellery and cave paintings.
当时早期现代人开始制造日益精巧的骨器和石器，在岩石上刻纹，并创作小雕像、首饰和洞穴壁画等具象艺术。
However, discoveries in Africa are pushing the origins of consumerism much further back into human prehistory.
但非洲的新发现正把消费文化的起源推到更久远的史前时期。
A few years ago, reports began to emerge of discoveries made at the Blombos Cave, a site of ancient human habitation in South Africa.
几年前，南非的一处古人类居住地布隆博斯洞穴陆续传出考古发现。

Christopher Henshilwood and colleagues from the University of Bergen in Norway dated thousands of pieces of ochre from the cave, and many of them proved to be more than 100,000 years old — before the time that early humans moved out of Africa.
挪威卑尔根大学的亨希尔伍德和同事测定了洞中数千块赭石的年代，其中许多已有十多万年历史，早于早期人类走出非洲。

Ochre, a coloured clay that comes in various shades from red to black, does not occur naturally around Blombos and must have been imported from quarries at least 30 kilometres away, either directly by Blombos residents or through trade.
赭石是一种颜色从红到黑不等的黏土，并非布隆博斯当地天然出产，居民要么亲自从至少三十公里外的采石点运回，要么通过交易获得。
Although ochre can be used to dry and preserve (cure) animal hides, the researchers are convinced the Blombos ochre had a symbolic purpose.
赭石虽可用于干燥和保存兽皮，但研究者相信洞内这些赭石具有象征用途。

For a start, it is predominantly red—any of the other colours available would have done for curing—and the surfaces of the clay had been scraped in a way that indicates they were used to yield pigment for dyes.
首先，它们多为红色，而处理兽皮用其他颜色也可以；其次，黏土表面的刮痕说明人们曾从中刮取染料用的颜料。
paragraphs.gist: 南非布隆博斯洞穴中有十多万年前从远处运来的赭石，多数偏红且带刮取颜料的痕迹，提示象征性消费可能早于原估年代。

paragraphs.brief: 古代贝珠与饰物的年代
sentences: An even more intriguing discovery from Blombos was of 41 beads dating from 76,000 years ago, found in clusters and made from the shells of a tiny mollusc.
布隆博斯还有一项更有趣的发现：四十一颗约七万六千年前的珠子，成簇出土，以微小软体动物的壳制成。
These cannot be natural deposits, argue the researchers, as each cluster contains shells of a similar size and colour with consistently placed holes.
研究者指出，这不会是自然堆积，因为每一簇内的贝壳大小、颜色相近，孔洞的位置也一致。
What’s more, all the beads display a pattern of wear suggesting friction from rubbing against thread, clothes or other beads.
此外，所有珠子都有磨损痕迹，像是长久与线、衣服或其他珠子摩擦造成的。
The previous oldest find of beads in Africa dates back to just 45,000 years ago.
此前非洲已知最古老的珠子仅可追溯到四万五千年前。
And it seems the Blombos people’s taste for beautiful items was not an isolated phenomenon.
布隆博斯人对美丽物品的喜爱，看来并非孤例。
Jessica Thompson of Arizona State University in Tempe has described finding shell fragments from a site in Tanzania that she believes may represent debris from bead manufacture.
亚利桑那州立大学的杰西卡·汤普森说，她在坦桑尼亚一处遗址发现贝壳碎片，推测可能是制珠留下的废料。
They are at least 45,000—and possibly 280,000—years old.
这些碎片至少已有四万五千年历史，甚至可能达到二十八万年。
Although there is no evidence of how the ancient beads were used, their modern counterparts are often traded.
虽然没有证据表明古代珠子是如何使用的，但现代珠子经常被交易。
So it looks as though our taste for jewellery and art is much older than we thought.
看来，人类喜爱珠宝与艺术的历史比我们原先认为的久远得多。
paragraphs.gist: 布隆博斯七万六千年前的贝珠大小相近、孔位一致并有摩擦痕，坦桑尼亚也有疑似制珠碎屑，显示偏爱饰物的历史可能很长。

paragraphs.brief: 从地位信物到社会等级
sentences: But why did we come to value these objects in the first place?
那么，我们究竟为什么会看重这些物件？
In many animal species, individuals signal their genetic fitness by showing off with attention-grabbing adornment.
在许多动物物种中，个体会展示引人注目的装饰，向同类显示自身的遗传适应度。
Some researchers think that in humans, consumer products play a similar role.
一些研究人员认为，在人类中，消费品也起着类似的作用。
Archaeologist Aimee Plourde, from the University of California, also argues that even in egalitarian societies, some people are more successful than others.
加利福尼亚大学考古学家Aimee Plourde也认为，即使在平等社会中，有些人也比其他人更成功。
Among our ancestors, superior skills in areas such as hunting, crafts, environmental knowledge and contact with neighbouring groups would have brought respect—in other words, prestige.
在祖先的社会中，狩猎、手工、了解环境或同邻近群体打交道等方面的出众本领，都可能让人赢得尊重，也就是声望。
And because prestige brings social benefits, people would want to show off their talents.
声望能带来社会上的好处，因此人们会希望让别人看见自己的本领。
The best way to do this would be through demonstrating possession of material items that are hard to fake.
一种很好的办法是展示自己拥有难以仿冒的实物。
‘A good hunter, for instance, could advertise his skills by wearing the tooth of an animal that is elusive or dangerous,’ says Plourde.
普卢尔德说：“例如，善于狩猎的人可以佩戴难以捕捉或十分危险的动物的牙齿，以此展示自己的本领。”
The benefits of prestige would also lead to competition to acquire it.
声望带来的好处也会引发争夺。
As a result, the value and variety of prestige goods would spiral and there would be a parallel increase in the ranking of social systems.
这样一来，地位物品的价值和种类会不断增加，社会的等级分化也会加深。
If Plourde is correct, prestige goods form a direct link between our innate drive for trade and the development of structured, hierarchical societies.
如果普劳德的解释成立，地位物品就把人天生的交易冲动与等级社会的发展直接联系起来。
They are arguably the first step on the road to modern civilisation, paving the way for agriculture and urbanisation.
可以说，它们是迈向现代文明的第一步，为农业和城市化铺平道路。
We may not be impressed by beads any more, but their modern equivalents have the same fascination.
珠子也许已不足以打动我们，但今天与它们相应的物品仍有同样的吸引力。
Nobody believes the guy who spends €670,000 on a Bugatti Veyron car does so because he needs to travel at 250 mph.
没有人会相信，一个人花 67 万欧元买一辆布加迪威龙，只是因为他需要以每小时 250 英里的速度行驶。
We all know in today’s consumer society he’s buying an exclusive status symbol.
在今天的消费社会中，大家都知道他买的是一种少数人才能拥有的地位象征。
paragraphs.gist: 普劳德推测，难以仿造的物品能替主人证明本领，围绕声望的竞争不断推高物品价值，也可能推动了社会等级和现代炫耀性消费的发展。

items.zh: 为 A 段选择最能概括全段的标题。
items.cue: 人类天生就会交易，无须商店或货币也能进行；商业的核心是人类学家所谓的“互惠”本能。
items.why: 即使不用钱，人也能记住谁给过谁什么，判断互换的物品是否相当。

items.zh: 为 B 段选择最能概括全段的标题。
items.answer: iii · Querying the changes in the value of traded items
items.solution: 追问交易物品的价值如何改变
items.cue: 贸易一旦开展，它带来的经济利益很快就让人难以抗拒。
items.why: 从交换生存必需品转向没有直接实用价值的物件，作者由此追问人何时开始珍视后者。

items.zh: 为 C 段选择最能概括全段的标题。
items.answer: vi · Recent finds alter theories about when consumerism started
items.solution: 新发现改变了对消费文化起源时间的判断
items.cue: 几年前，南非的一处古人类居住地布隆博斯洞穴陆续传出考古发现。
items.why: 非洲发现的赭石等遗存把象征性消费的线索推到早于以往设想的年代。

items.zh: 为 D 段选择最能概括全段的标题。
items.answer: ii · The clues that indicate ancient items were decorative
items.solution: 表明古物用于装饰的线索
items.cue: 布隆博斯还有一项更有趣的发现：四十一颗约七万六千年前的珠子，成簇出土，以微小软体动物的壳制成。
items.why: 贝珠的来源、穿孔及磨损模式提示它们经过选择并曾被串戴。

items.zh: 为 E 段选择最能概括全段的标题。
items.answer: v · How status can be gained from ownership of goods
items.solution: 拥有物品如何带来社会地位
items.cue: 如果普劳德的解释成立，地位物品就把人天生的交易冲动与等级社会的发展直接联系起来。
items.why: 稀有物件能展示狩猎等技能，拥有者借此获得声望及其社会好处。

options: The desire to make expensive jewellery
珠饰是讨论何时赋予物品象征价值的证据，文中没有把制作昂贵首饰当作远古人的明确愿望。
The clues that indicate ancient items were decorative
表明古物用于装饰的线索
贝珠的来源、穿孔及磨损模式提示它们经过选择并曾被串戴。
Querying the changes in the value of traded items
追问交易物品的价值如何改变
从交换生存必需品转向没有直接实用价值的物件，作者由此追问人何时开始珍视后者。
即使不用钱，人也能记住谁给过谁什么，判断互换的物品是否相当。
How status can be gained from ownership of goods
拥有物品如何带来社会地位
稀有物件能展示狩猎等技能，拥有者借此获得声望及其社会好处。
Recent finds alter theories about when consumerism started
新发现改变了对消费文化起源时间的判断
非洲发现的赭石等遗存把象征性消费的线索推到早于以往设想的年代。
文中改变时间推断的是较早的考古发现，未描写研究方法本身革新。
flow: 从互惠交换问到物品价值
人能记住谁给予了什么，但当交换对象从必需品变成装饰物，就需要解释人为何会珍视它们。
用颜料和贝珠追查早期装饰
非洲遗址把象征性消费的时间往前推，贝珠的穿孔和磨痕又让研究者辨认出串戴的痕迹。
用地位解释稀有物品的价值
若稀有物品能让旁人看到持有者的本领，它就能带来声望，也回应了开头关于价值的问题。

items.en: In section A, ‘reciprocity’ refers to our ancestors’ ability to
items.zh: A 段的“互惠”是指祖先具备哪种能力？
correct: monitor the balance between goods given and received
记住自己付出和得到的物品，并判断两者是否相当。

items.en: What is said about the ochre found at Blombos Cave?
items.zh: 作者怎样描述布隆博斯洞穴出土的赭石？
correct: It appears it was selected for its colour.
人们似乎依据颜色挑选了这些赭石。

items.en: What made the researchers realise the purpose of the beads found at Blombos Cave?
items.zh: 布隆博斯洞穴出土的珠子上有什么线索，让研究者推断出它们的用途？
correct: They have holes and markings suggesting they were joined together.
珠子上的孔和磨痕表明它们曾被串在一起。

items.en: Some researchers argue that we may use ownership of desirable goods to demonstrate our strength and fitness as other ________ use their attractive physical features.
items.zh: 有研究者认为，人类通过拥有令人向往的物品彰显实力和适应能力，正如其他________展示富有吸引力的身体特征。
items.why: 定位句说：“在许多动物物种中，个体会展示引人注目的装饰，向同类显示自身的遗传适应度。”

items.en: Showing off one’s superiority is not a new phenomenon and even in ancient times successful people would have gained ________ from this.
items.zh: 炫耀自身优势并非新鲜事。即使在古代，成功者也可能借此赢得________。
items.why: “展示优越” 带来别人对你的“尊重/声望”"。词表给出 respect,与原文同义词组“prestige”并列印证。

items.en: A desire for status could have led to an increase in the worth of prestige goods and to ________ among people wishing to achieve this status.
items.zh: 人们追求社会地位，可能抬高象征身份的物品的价值，也可能使争取这种地位的人之间出现________。
items.why: 定位句说：“声望带来的好处也会引发争夺。”

items.en: It is thought that our natural desire to trade provided a basis for organised farming and ________ development and finally resulted in the complex societies which can be seen today.
items.zh: 人们认为，交易的天性为有组织的农业和________发展奠定了基础，最终促成今天这样复杂的社会。
items.why: urbanisation = 城市化/城市发展，填入 city 形成自然搭配“city development (城市发展)”。(比 settlements development 更地道，也与“urbanisation” 严格同义。)

items.en: Whilst we do not value things such as beads nowadays, other items hold the same appeal for us and bring the same status as owning beads did for our ________.
items.zh: 如今我们并不看重珠子，但其他物品同样吸引我们，也能带来当年珠子为我们的________所带来的地位。
items.why: 句式对比“古代珠子"与“现代等价物",所指对象是“祖先"。词表给出 ancestors。

groups.instructionsZh: 先回想空格里的英文。每空填一个词。

pairs: 题干用名词，定位句改用同词根的形容词。
points: 从交换生存必需品转向没有直接实用价值的物件，作者由此追问人何时开始珍视后者。

clauses: …, the economic benefits quickly make it irresistible.
连接词 once 引出“Once trade gets off the ground”，说明主句的时间关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 once 把这一层关系补进去。
…, the researchers are convinced the Blombos ochre had a symbolic purpose.
连接词 although 引出“Although ochre can be used to dry and preserve (cure) animal hides”，说明主句的让步关系。

lead: Long before our ancestors had any trappings of civilisation, they had a taste for material goods.
早在我们的祖先有任何文明的陷阱之前，他们就有了对物质品的品味。
Kate Douglas discovers where this ancient obsession has led us.
凯特·道格拉斯发现了古老的迷恋把我们引向何方
